newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian credit policy may not affect rupee - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Indian credit policy may not affect rupee - analysts.

text.p: India's central bank monetary policy, to be unveiled on Saturday, is unlikely to affect the foreign exchange market in a major way, forex brokers and bankers said on Friday.
The Reserve Bank of India unveils its monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March) on October 19.
"The market does not expect any significant measures (in the policy) which will affect spot rates," said the treasury head of a state-run bank.
"Dollar supplies are steady while there doesn't seem to be much demand... the rupee-dollar rate should remain steady."
Expectations of easing domestic liquidity following a cut in cash reserve ratios (CRR) have already been discounted by the market, dealers said.
"Forward premia have bottomed out as the market has discounted the possibility of a one percentage point cut in CRR," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
If the monetary policy was on expected lines with a cut in CRR to 11 percent from 12 percent, forward premia could firm up slightly on profit-taking, he said.
However as domestic liquidity eased on lower CRR, forward premia would remain low, he said.
If the expected cut in CRR did not come about, the forward market would react sharply and premia would harden, he said.
